title: Ensuring health equity with the use of AI
description: Only 13% of articles examined in a review of artificial intelligence (AI) and health equity explicitly defined health equity—a gap that could leave AI-driven approaches benefiting the most advantaged groups. That's a key finding from a review led by Caroline R. Efird of Georgetown University and colleagues. The research was published Oct. 8, 2026, in Health Affairs Scholar.

title: Dartmouth Provost Who Warned About AI Cheating Resigns After Investigation of His Own AI Usage
